label: Grouped bf16 experts
mechanism: the one MoE layer the NVFP4 export skipped moves from the per-hit-expert reference loop to the same grouped GEMM every other MoE layer already uses, which deletes the device sync that forced it out of the captured decode step
hypothesis: Layer 2 (dense_mlp_idx) is the ONE MoE layer whose routed experts ship bf16-unquantized (CLAUDE.md model facts; hf_quant_config exclude list; census B1.2/B1.3), so it is the one MoE layer that never got exp-0003's grouped GEMM: model.moe_experts falls through to the reference loop, `for e in torch.unique(topk_indices).tolist()` plus one pair of GEMMs per hit expert. At the canonical concurrency that is a device->host sync per traversal and ~2 x 200 launches serving 1-2 rows each. exp-0012 could not capture it, so it carved layer 2 out as the eager island graphrun._run_island and split device 0 into TWO graphs around it; exp-0018's spec named folding that island into the graph as the ranked-next attack. ONE VARIABLE: a bf16 twin of kernels/moe_gemm.py (kernels/moe_gemm_bf16.py) — same sorted-pair list, same searchsorted segment offsets (never bincount: its CUDA path sizes the histogram from self.max().cpu(), the hidden sync exp-0015b had to remove), same grid (E, N/BLOCK_N) with empty-expert programs exiting immediately, same epilogue rounding chain, same tile constants; the only layout differences are that w13's [gates; ups] halves are already de-interleaved here (gate row n, up row FFN+n) and that there are no scales to apply. Because the twin is sync-free and fixed-shape, model.experts_capturable() — the SINGLE predicate both model.py and graphrun.py read, so the two sites cannot disagree about what got captured — now returns True for layer 2, graphrun.islands goes [2] -> [] and device 0 captures as ONE segment. MEASURED IN SITU, not extrapolated (exp-0011's rejection is the standing reminder that the island's host work deliberately runs in the shadow of the surrounding replays, so isolation overstates it): engine/pyengine/tests/t_bf16_island.py, one resident load, GraphRunner rebuilt per arm, a DISCARDED warm-up arm first (the first arm in a process pays whole-traversal JIT — it alone made prefill read 36.3 s vs 6.4 s warm) then interleaved island/grouped/island/grouped so any residual trend cancels. Mean decode step at 64 concurrent requests: island 228.7 / 225.8 ms, grouped 214.6 / 216.4 ms -> 227.2 -> 215.5 ms, -11.7 ms/step (1.054x), a delta 4x the 2.9 ms repeat spread; min-step 185.8/185.5 -> 175.3/175.2 agrees at -10.4 ms. Structure asserted in the same run: islands [2] -> [], captured segments 5 -> 4. Isolated (tests/t_moe_bf16.py, real checkpoint shapes E=256/ffn=3072/hidden=6144, synthetic weights) the layer's MoE half goes 23.66 -> 3.39 ms at decode T=65 and 32.53 -> 4.77 ms at prefill T=745; the grouped number is ~6.7 TB/s against the ~22.6 GiB of bf16 expert weight the ~200 hit experts must stream, i.e. near the HBM roofline, while the loop ran at ~0.96 TB/s. The 20.3 ms isolated decode delta versus the 11.7 ms in-situ delta is the island's shadowed host time, and the in-situ number is the one this spec predicts on.
predicted_delta: +2.0 to +4.5% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s over the best same-protocol accepted row 221.8 (merge bar 222.5): point estimate ~231, floor ~226. Cycle model, stated so it can be falsified: exp-0018's model of the accepted 221.8 row (~180 prefill traversals x 1.373 s = 247 s + 2166 decode steps x 0.168 s = 364 s = 611 s, reproducing that row within 2%) gives 2166 x 11.7 ms = 25.3 s off a 611 s box = +4.3% -> 231.3. The floor comes from the one term the model cannot pin: the measured -11.7 ms is position-INDEPENDENT (it is MoE weight traffic, not attention), so on canonical decode_heavy, where OSL ~8K drives L_pad and the global-attention term up, it is a SHRINKING fraction of a growing step — at an exp-0012-class 330 ms step it is 3.5%, and if the decode term is only ~60% of the box it is ~2.1%. Prefill: the isolated arm says -27.8 ms per layer-2 traversal, but the in-situ 64-sequence prefill wall was 6.4 s in BOTH arms, i.e. the effect is below this test's 0.1 s resolution once exp-0017 cohort-admission has folded 64 sequences into ~11 traversals, so NO prefill win is claimed here. Rejection case: if the whole delta lands inside noise the row sits at ~222 and the result still says the island's host cost was fully shadowed after all — which would be the first direct measurement of that, and would retire attack #4 rather than leave it ranked.

local_pregate.tf_gate: GREEN, /workspace/logs/tf_gate_exp0019.log — parity_pass true. agree 383/400 = 0.9575 vs floor 0.945 (D13: envelope 0.965 - 2 pts), delta_mean 0.056637 vs bar 0.067851 (envelope 0.054281 x 1.25), delta_max 1.336095. Live server on GPUs 4-7, port 8219, --tf-positions 8 against experiments/tf_envelope.json. READ THIS HONESTLY: agreement IMPROVED on the accepted lineage's 379/400, but delta_mean rose from its 0.043856 to 0.056637 and now sits at 83% of the bar. The two arms trade off by construction — delta_mean is averaged over AGREEING positions only (harness/correctness.py:157-160), so the 4 positions that newly agree are marginal ones that enter the pool carrying large |dlogprob|, and delta_max 1.336 is one of them. The residual rise is ordinary depth-amplified accumulation-order drift: layer 2's output moves by rel_mean 2.5e-3 / cos 0.99999 (arm a) and then passes through 63 more layers. It is the B3.1/B3.3 drift class the D13 envelope exists to bound, not a precision regression — the twin applies no quantization the loop did not, and its slot reduction is fp32 where the loop's index_add_ was bf16. Flagged because the headroom is now 17%, so a future experiment that also perturbs prefill numerics should expect to be the one that runs out of it.

NOT bitwise, and cannot be (B3.1/B3.3): the drift sources are fp32 GEMM accumulation ORDER and the per-token slot-sum, exactly the two the packed path already contributes on the other 63 MoE layers. In situ (t_bf16_island.py) island-vs-grouped token streams agree bitwise on 13/64 rows with the rest diverging from step 0 — the same envelope-drift signature exp-0012's own eager-vs-graph arm reports.
local_pregate.determinism: TWO arms, both green. (i) tests/t_moe_bf16.py arm b: two identical grouped calls bitwise equal at both shapes. (ii) tests/t_bf16_island.py: two full 64-request runs of the SAME schedule produce bitwise-identical token streams (hard assert), and the island arm is asserted repeatable against itself the same way. Sources of nondeterminism were designed out rather than tested away: stable sort, exact-integer searchsorted offsets, fixed grids, no atomics, every output row written exactly once.
local_pregate.capture_safety: arm c of tests/t_moe_bf16.py, the property the whole experiment turns on: the grouped call is captured inside torch.cuda.graph and replayed, bitwise equal to the eager result on the same inputs, at both decode and prefill shapes. Confirmed end-to-end in situ — graphrun.islands is [2] under PYENGINE_BF16_GROUPED=0 and [] under =1, captured segments 5 -> 4, and the graphed arms ran 39 decode steps per arm across a live 512->1024 L_pad re-capture.
